title: Authenticator Assurance Level Evaluator
description: Rates whether a declared authenticator set and session policy reach a target level of a caller-supplied, versioned authentication assurance framework. Framework-agnostic: every threshold and restriction is input data, never hardcoded. Distinguishes a definition that cannot express a criterion (AAL_DEFINITION_INSUFFICIENT) from declared data that fails a well-formed one (AAL_SHORTFALL, reported per criterion as {criterion, required, found}).

framework.description: Versioned assurance framework: levels[] ordered lowest-to-highest, each carrying criteria in the shared generic vocabulary (min_factors, required_factor_kinds, phishing_resistant_required, verifier_impersonation_resistant_required, hardware_bound_required, dynamic_authentication_required, max_reauth_interval_minutes, max_idle_minutes, restricted_authenticator_kinds)

target_level.description: level_id of the target level within the declared framework

authenticators.description: Declared authenticator set; kind values from the node's closed enum, factor_kinds from the caller's own category vocabulary (tested for set membership only)

session.description: Optional declared session policy; reauthentication and idle intervals in minutes

mcp_tool_definition.name: compute_authn_assurance_level
mcp_tool_definition.description: Given a versioned framework (levels[] ordered lowest-to-highest, each carrying generic authentication criteria), a declared authenticators[] set from the node kind enum, a declared session policy, and a target_level, return achieved_level, meets_target, per-criterion unmet_criteria as {criterion, required, found}, compliance flags, and the framework_ref.

author: PostOakLabs

output_example.note: Rates a DECLARED authenticator set and session policy against a caller-supplied, versioned assurance framework -- never a hardcoded one. Every threshold, required factor category and restriction comes from the framework the caller declares; the kernel never interprets a framework it was not given. A criterion the definition cannot express (malformed criterion value) is reported as AAL_DEFINITION_INSUFFICIENT, distinct from AAL_SHORTFALL (declared data failing a well-formed criterion, reported per criterion as {criterion, required, found}) -- the two are never conflated. When the target level is not met, achieved_level falls back to the highest fully-met level below it. Measures declared capabilities only: it does not assert anyone controls any authenticator, and carries no user identifiers.
